html:
The Mayaimi were a Native people who lived around Lake Okeechobee in southern Florida from the start of the Common Era until the 1600s or 1700s. In their language, as in that of the Calusa and Tequesta, Mayaimi meant "big water", and the name passed to the Miami River and the city of Miami.

They belonged to what archaeologists call the Belle Glade culture, and built earthworks, mounds and canals around the lake. They fished and hunted in the wetlands. Almost all that is written about them comes from Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, a Spanish boy shipwrecked in 1549 who lived for seventeen years among the Calusa. Disease and slave raids from the north destroyed the Mayaimi in the 1700s.
